representation minor in H
content:
‘I have always been extraordinarily interested in Peter Behrens 'Technical Administration Building of Hoechst AG'. If a drawing is meant to have near absolute congruence with what it is representing, this project has always been fascinating to me because the divergence between the drawn and the executed was almost extraordinary. The drawings are very plain, the projection, simple. But the brickwork is almost transcendental in alignment and color. If anything it's a question of specificity, of how much can be compressed into a drawing - and this question has been complicated extraordinarily by BIM, where the answer is, an almost infinite amount of detail, and yet clearly the problem did not in fact lay in the raw *amount* of data that the drawing could compress.’

‘Indeed, it is not difficult to suggest that the divide between the representation and the thing-in-itself will remain just as such, if the thing cannot be exhausted and so represented fully.’
